issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end`, but the solution implementation uses the label `end_loop`. The template does not provide any `loop_end` label either. This inconsistency between the problem text and the solution's label name can confuse students when they try to follow the instructions or compare their work to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent. Update the solution's label from `end_loop` to `loop_end` (or update the problem statement to require `end_loop` -> `end_loop`) so that problem instructions, template expectations, and the solution all use the same label name. Ensure the template or solution contains the requested `loop_end` label to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement requires marking the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end`, but the solution uses the label `end_loop`. This names the same conceptual entity (the end-of-loop label) differently across artifacts, which can confuse students when they compare their work, the instructions, and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent label name across all artifacts. Change the solution's label `end_loop` to `loop_end` (or update the problem statement to request `end_loop`) and, if helpful, add the `loop_end` label in the template at the intended location so students see the exact name to use.
